passages.note: A reporter's story quoting Randolph against jailing homeless people; the article's account of the chamber votes is not a record (H15) and the excerpt names no bill number.

rows.reasoning: Randolph's own words — “That’s not the answer. The answer is helping these homeless people by providing the things that they need, like food, shelter and a job — not jail time.” — put him against “Banning public camping and sleeping with criminal penalties to maintain public safety and order”, but they name no mechanism that separates “Protecting the right to sleep and shelter in public spaces, with no penalties of any kind” from “Decriminalizing public sleeping and camping in public spaces” or from “Allowing enforcement only when adequate shelter beds are available, with citations diverting people to services rather than the criminal justice system”. He says nothing about whether any enforcement, citation or civil penalty may remain, so the passage shows a side only.
